issue: A notification authorized for one persisted job attempt could mutate a newer attempt because service dispatch passed only JobId after authorization.

reproduction.scope: Actual Room and ReconstructionExecutionController calls matching the service dispatch sequence, not execution of Android Service scheduling or Intent decoding.
sequence: Enqueue attempt 0 and authorize its CANCEL notification.
Acquire the actual Room job lease, creating attempt 1.
Invoke the original controller.cancel(JobId) after authorization.
Require replacement attempt to remain RUNNING with its original lease.

semantics: Reauthorize the original notification identity and current allowed state in the same Room transaction as the mutation.
Use the transaction-current attempt and stateVersion with existing commandIfCurrent; harmless same-attempt progress or lease renewal does not invalidate identity.
For pause/cancel, capture only an exact matching operation token with equal token reads around job/attempt reads; never cancel the generic current worker.
Preserve existing pause/cancel presentation ownership when another job runs.
Service schedules resume drain only after accepted dispatch; controller adds no duplicate foreground-service start.

greenCases: Reject an old authorized notification after a new attempt acquires the lease.
Accept current pause/resume/cancel after same-attempt lease renewal.
Cancel another queued job without replacing running-job presentation or lease; reflection sets presentation ownership only, not a native token.
limits: Native exact-token signaling is source-reviewed only; these HOST tests do not launch a JNI kernel.
Actual Android Service scheduling, PendingIntent delivery, device notification interaction and physical-device behavior remain untested by this regression.
No generic job-store semantics or unrelated UI command path is changed.

delivery.interpretation: The delivered APK predates this narrow race fix; this is not a blanket unsafe-app claim.
